── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: You caught a cold with a fever, so this week is a gentle return, not a catch-up. …
Answers: No, please do not. After a fever you want fewer runs than usual for a week or so, not more, and piling on missed sessions is the fastest way to a setback or a relapse.
Safety flag: Check in with your doctor if the cough lingers
Next week:
Mon: easy, walk-run 21 min, 7 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, keep the run segments…
Tue: rest, a walk with the dog is fine. Recovery day.
Wed: easy, walk-run 24 min, 8 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, same effort as Monday. Returns…
Thu: rest. Keeps a full day between runs while you rebuild.
Fri: rest. Sets up Saturday to feel strong.
Sat: easy, walk-run 27 min, 9 x 2 min run and 1 min walk, only if Mon and Wed felt good…
Sun: rest. Full recovery before next week.
